citations.quote: Figure S18 presents the longer cycling performance of $MoS_{2}$ , conducted to further confirm the extended durability and stability of the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. More importantly, $MoS_{2}$ cycled at $0.5\;A\;g^{-1}$ in the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte maintains a high reversible specific capacity of $60.6\;mAh\;g^{-1}$ even after 300 cycles, with an average CE reaching 99.7%. To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ was examined at $10\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell under a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ still exhibits a high specific capacity of $42.7\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity. Furthermore, no obvious enhancement in polarization during charging and discharging is observed, indicating stable interphases and no obvious side reactions in the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cells using 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. Figure 5I illustrates the $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ -solvates interfacial behaviors in the optimized 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, showing reduced desolvation energy and enhanced transfer kinetics across a broad temperature range.

citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

In summary, these results confirm that the NTM electrolyte simultaneously constructs NaF-rich and stable interfaces on both the NVP cathode and HC anode within full cells. The synergistic optimization of both cathode and anode interfaces is the fundamental origin of the battery's excellent electrochemical performance. The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

citations.chunk_id: 0038_Liu 等 - 2024 - Ester-based anti-freezing electrolyte achieving ultra-low temperature cycling for sodium-ion batteri::sec11
citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

citations.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

With decreasing temperature, batteries experience significantly increased interfacial impedance and pronounced capacity decay, closely linked to the desolvation and migration of $Na^{+}$ through the SEI [50,51]. Therefore, achieving excellent Na storage properties at subzero temperatures hinges on minimizing the desolvation energy of $Na^{+}$ [52]. Temperature-dependent conductivity and viscosity measurements reveal that NaOTF-G2 exhibits superior low-temperature performance compared to $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ and $NaPF_{6}-G2$ (Figure S15). While $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ shows higher conductivity above $-20^{\circ}C$ due to its low viscosity, it solidifies upon cooling, leading to a sharp decline in ionic mobility. In contrast, NaOTF-G2 maintains a conductivity of $1.02\ mS\ cm^{-1}$ at $-40^{\circ}C$ , attributed to weak $Na^{+}-OTF^{-}$ coordination and favorable solvation dynamics that suppress salt aggregation and freezing. These properties ensure sustained ion transport and stable interfacial chemistry even under extreme cold conditions. Thanks to the low-solvation electrolytes and homogeneous SEI, the NaOTF-G2 system achieves competitive performance even at the extremely low temperature of $-40^{\circ}C$ (Figure 5A). This temperature still represents a relevant low-temperature regime and provides meaningful insight consistent with the experimental results. After 100 cycles, an excellent capacity retention of 78.5% can still be achieved. PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Abstract Hard carbon (HC) remains the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its low initial Coulombic efficiency and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) hinder long-term performance. Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Here we propose a “revitalization” strategy to clarify the synergistic influence of solvent and anion chemistry by systematically evaluating three electrolytes: 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in diethylene glycol dimethyl ether ( $NaPF_{6}-G2$ ), and 1.0 M sodium trifluoromethanesulfonate in G2 (NaOTF-G2). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

With increasing sputtering time, NaF gradually becomes the dominant component, forming a bilayer solid-electrolyte interlayer (SEI) structure consisting of an inorganic-rich inner layer and an organic-rich outer layer. In summary, these results confirm that the NTM electrolyte simultaneously constructs NaF-rich and stable interfaces on both the NVP cathode and HC anode within full cells. 4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

evidence_ledger.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . citations.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

citations.quote: Figure S18 presents the longer cycling performance of $MoS_{2}$ , conducted to further confirm the extended durability and stability of the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. More importantly, $MoS_{2}$ cycled at $0.5\;A\;g^{-1}$ in the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte maintains a high reversible specific capacity of $60.6\;mAh\;g^{-1}$ even after 300 cycles, with an average CE reaching 99.7%. To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ was examined at $10\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell under a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ still exhibits a high specific capacity of $42.7\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity. Furthermore, no obvious enhancement in polarization during charging and discharging is observed, indicating stable interphases and no obvious side reactions in the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cells using 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. Figure 5I illustrates the $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ -solvates interfacial behaviors in the optimized 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, showing reduced desolvation energy and enhanced transfer kinetics across a broad temperature range.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

With increasing sputtering time, NaF gradually becomes the dominant component, forming a bilayer solid-electrolyte interlayer (SEI) structure consisting of an inorganic-rich inner layer and an organic-rich outer layer. In summary, these results confirm that the NTM electrolyte simultaneously constructs NaF-rich and stable interfaces on both the NVP cathode and HC anode within full cells. The synergistic optimization of both cathode and anode interfaces is the fundamental origin of the battery's excellent electrochemical performance. Furthermore, the high- and low-temperature electrochemical performance of the electrolytes was evaluated in full-cell configurations. This enhanced stability primarily arises from the formation of NaF-enriched gradient CEI/SEI layers, which effectively suppress electrolyte decomposition at elevated temperatures.

PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

association_citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec4::child0
association_citations.quote: The electrochemical performance of NTM was evaluated using assembled NVP||Na half-cells at 25 °C. As depicted in Figures 3a and S11 (Supporting Information), the NVP||Na cell cycled in NTM electrolyte displays superior cycling performance, maintaining a high-capacity retention of 91.8% even after 400 cycles, significantly outperforming those with NT and NP electrolytes (NP retains 83.4% after 200 cycles). In addition, the NTM electrolyte exhibits excellent rate performance, retaining a capacity of up to 92.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ at a current density of 2000 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure 3b; Figure S12, Supporting Information). The NVP||Na with NTM electrolyte also exhibits excellent stability at a cut-off voltage of 4.5 V, achieving a capacity retention of 97.5% and a stable Coulombic efficiency above 99.6% (Figure S13, Supporting Information). In addition, the Fe-based Prussian blue||Na battery employing the NTM electrolyte also exhibits excellent cycling stability, demonstrating its universality (Figure S14, Supporting Information). The observed electrochemical performance variations among the three electrolytes likely arise from the distinct composition and morphology of NVP interfaces, resulting from differences in electrolyte formulation and solvation structures. Detailed X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis was conducted to elucidate the interfacial layer composition and structure.

association_citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child0
association_citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

citations.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

Abstract Hard carbon (HC) remains the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its low initial Coulombic efficiency and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) hinder long-term performance. Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Here we propose a “revitalization” strategy to clarify the synergistic influence of solvent and anion chemistry by systematically evaluating three electrolytes: 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in diethylene glycol dimethyl ether ( $NaPF_{6}-G2$ ), and 1.0 M sodium trifluoromethanesulfonate in G2 (NaOTF-G2). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . citations.chunk_id: 0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec8::child0
citations.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

citations.quote: Figure S18 presents the longer cycling performance of $MoS_{2}$ , conducted to further confirm the extended durability and stability of the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. More importantly, $MoS_{2}$ cycled at $0.5\;A\;g^{-1}$ in the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte maintains a high reversible specific capacity of $60.6\;mAh\;g^{-1}$ even after 300 cycles, with an average CE reaching 99.7%. To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ was examined at $10\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell under a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ still exhibits a high specific capacity of $42.7\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity. Furthermore, no obvious enhancement in polarization during charging and discharging is observed, indicating stable interphases and no obvious side reactions in the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cells using 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. Figure 5I illustrates the $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ -solvates interfacial behaviors in the optimized 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, showing reduced desolvation energy and enhanced transfer kinetics across a broad temperature range.

citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2
citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

citations.quote: The XPS results of the HC anode reveal a higher proportion of inorganic NaF species in NTM system (Figures S38 and S39, Supporting Information). With increasing sputtering time, NaF gradually becomes the dominant component, forming a bilayer solid-electrolyte interlayer (SEI) structure consisting of an inorganic-rich inner layer and an organic-rich outer layer. In summary, these results confirm that the NTM electrolyte simultaneously constructs NaF-rich and stable interfaces on both the NVP cathode and HC anode within full cells. The synergistic optimization of both cathode and anode interfaces is the fundamental origin of the battery's excellent electrochemical performance. Furthermore, the high- and low-temperature electrochemical performance of the electrolytes was evaluated in full-cell configurations. The results reveal that the NTM system retains 67.8 mA h g $^{-1}$ (77.8% retention) after 100 cycles at 50 °C, whereas the NP system exhibits only 61.7% retention with more pronounced fading (Figure 5f; Figure S40, Supporting Information). The NTM system also demonstrates stable cycling behavior at 80 °C (Figure S41, Supporting Information). This enhanced stability primarily arises from the formation of NaF-enriched gradient CEI/SEI layers, which effectively suppress electrolyte decomposition at elevated temperatures.

association_citations.quote: The electrochemical performance of NTM was evaluated using assembled NVP||Na half-cells at 25 °C. As depicted in Figures 3a and S11 (Supporting Information), the NVP||Na cell cycled in NTM electrolyte displays superior cycling performance, maintaining a high-capacity retention of 91.8% even after 400 cycles, significantly outperforming those with NT and NP electrolytes (NP retains 83.4% after 200 cycles). In addition, the NTM electrolyte exhibits excellent rate performance, retaining a capacity of up to 92.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ at a current density of 2000 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure 3b; Figure S12, Supporting Information). The NVP||Na with NTM electrolyte also exhibits excellent stability at a cut-off voltage of 4.5 V, achieving a capacity retention of 97.5% and a stable Coulombic efficiency above 99.6% (Figure S13, Supporting Information). In addition, the Fe-based Prussian blue||Na battery employing the NTM electrolyte also exhibits excellent cycling stability, demonstrating its universality (Figure S14, Supporting Information). The observed electrochemical performance variations among the three electrolytes likely arise from the distinct composition and morphology of NVP interfaces, resulting from differences in electrolyte formulation and solvation structures. Detailed X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis was conducted to elucidate the interfacial layer composition and structure.

4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

citations.chunk_id: 0038_Liu 等 - 2024 - Ester-based anti-freezing electrolyte achieving ultra-low temperature cycling for sodium-ion batteri::sec10::child6
citations.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

### 逆向设计例外：先诊断，筛选仅决定能否推荐配方

对于容量骤降、首圈库仑效率低、高压衰减、阻抗增长等 `inverse_design` 问题，先从检索证据中建立至少两个可区分的电解液侧假设，并提出能区分它们的 EIS、Raman、XPS、LSV、ICP、产气或对照实验。仍执行候选配方筛选，但筛选 `hold` 只禁止“推荐进入实验”的完整配方；不得因此省略诊断、混杂因素和条件化调整方向。报告必须区分“已被证据支持的诊断事实”与“待验证的调整方向”。

1. 解析用户目标与约束；把用户要求的每项条件写成结构化 `constraint_records`，例如：
   不得把整段用户问题放入 `target_conditions`，再把旧文本检查识别到的部分词语当成全部要求。
   推荐前逐项核对用户要求与检查条件，避免漏掉正极、负极、电池形式、温度、倍率或指标定义。
   检索前先解释用户给出的数值条件：它描述什么物理量、单位如何理解、哪些信息尚不明确。
   这一解释依据用户描述的工作场景，在检索前定下，不能由后来检索到的论文或知识图谱记录
   反过来改写；其它论文里恰好出现同样的 “N C” 写法，只说明那些论文的用法，不能用来判断
   用户这句话。
   温度与倍率的单位必须分清。省略度符号的 C 不能直接视为充放电倍率。
   按它在句中的位置判断：直接修饰电芯、电池或其使用环境时（如 “a pouch cell at -30 C”、
   “a full cell around 50 C”），是温度；只有与充放电动作或倍率词连用时
   （如 “discharged at 1 C”、“cycled at 0.5 C”、“1 C rate”），才是倍率。
   按上下文确定一种解释后，就用这一种建立约束，
   不因缺少度符号再补一条互斥的倍率或温度约束，也不因检索结果改回另一种解释。
   检索查询和筛选断言须明确写出所采用的
   物理量与单位。只有上下文确实无法确定物理量时，才同时列出两种解释并说明需要澄清，
   此时暂缓推荐，而不是把两种解释同时写成两条互斥的数值约束。
   接近目标温度的文献结果应保留实测温度，不能改写为目标温度。
   硬约束来自用户问题，不得自行加上某一正极、软包形式、长循环寿命或数值阈值。
   在若干可替代选项之间尚未确定时（例如某类溶剂或某类盐有多种候选），不得把它们
   同时写成必需的 `required_component`；每个选项应作为独立候选分别比较，不叠加互斥的必需组分。
   近似目标也必须进入筛选，不得因用户没有给出容差而省略。保留用户对目标的原话，
   用现有 `evidence_claim` 表达候选须有相应工况下的直接测试依据，而非把近似目标
   改成精确相等、单边不等式或自行设定容差。逐候选判断时，`supported` 须引用该
   候选的实际测试条件与性能原句，`basis` 写清实测条件与目标的差别及其关联依据。
   只有其他工况的结果、测试建议或机理预测时，不能据此判近似工况要求已满足。
   没有相应测试依据就保留 `not_found` 并补证，不能删掉该要求后批准推荐，再把它
   放进 `next_steps`。有邻近条件下的直接依据时，在报告中明确实际条件与目标的
   差别，精确目标下的后续验证可以另列。电极、电池形式和其他明确要求仍须检查。
   联合条件也须保留近似目标的含义：不得把近似值写成 `target_context` 中要求
   精确匹配的数值。近似工况及其电极、全电池归属可写在同一 `evidence_claim`
   中，引用实际共同测试的结果；组分身份等与工况无关的要求不并入该测试条件组。
   “低成本”等定性目标须区分文献提出的成本动机与已量化的价格优势；未提供价格数据
   时不得称已验证低成本。数值明确的用户要求仍按原值建立硬约束，不得因此放宽。
   无法从问题得出数值判据的定性目标，保留为选材目标，在报告中说明依据和待验证
   条件。定性或近似目标通过断言及其原文依据判断，不变成必须命中字面词的关键词条件。
   这不允许省略用户明确给出的电极、电池形式、精确温度或倍率要求。
   当用户目标包含某项性能指标（如 capacity retention relative to room-temperature
   capacity、离子电导率、倍率性能、首圈库仑效率），先分清用户给的是**数值阈值**还是
   **只要报告**：给了明确数值时写成对应数值约束——保持率用 `minimum_retention`、
   电导率用 `minimum_conductivity`、倍率用 `c_rate`，`value` 取用户给出的数值；
   只要求“报告该指标”“有无该结果”而未给数值时，不得把阈值填 0 了事——`value: 0`
   会让任何数字都通过，等于没有检查。这类“须被报告/须成立”的指标改用
   `kind: "evidence_claim"`（见下），把该指标写成一句断言。
   `field_presence` 只用于检查候选的配方字段（`concentration_mol_l`、
   `solvent_ratios`、`additives` 等）是否显式填写，绝不用于表达“某项性能必须被报告”。
   禁止把“capacity retention … must be reported”写成
   `"kind": "field_presence", "field": "additives"` 这类把性能指标错配到配方字段的约束。
   ```json
   {
     "request": {
       "candidates": candidates,
       "constraint_records": [
         {
           "constraint_id": "temp-low",
           "description": "operating temperature ≤ -20°C",
           "kind": "temperature",
           "operator": "<=",
           "value": -20,
           "unit": "°C",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find low-temperature cycling evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "electrode-hard-carbon",
           "description": "hard carbon anode",
           "kind": "electrode_material",
           "evidence_terms": ["hard carbon", "hard-carbon"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find hard carbon anode evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "cell-half",
           "description": "sodium half-cell configuration",
           "kind": "cell_configuration",
           "evidence_terms": ["half-cell", "half cell", "Na||HC", "HC||Na", "pure Na"],
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find half-cell configuration evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "field-concentration",
           "description": "explicit salt concentration must be present",
           "kind": "field_presence",
           "field": "concentration_mol_l",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": false
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "salt-napf6",
           "description": "NaPF6 as salt",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "NaPF6",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find NaPF6 electrolyte evidence"
         },
         {
           "constraint_id": "solvent-thf",
           "description": "THF as solvent",
           "kind": "required_component",
           "value": "THF",
           "required_evidence_scope": "candidate_same_paper",
           "can_replan": true,
           "search_hint": "find THF solvent evidence"
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```
   定性或断言型要求（如“无集流体/壳体腐蚀被观测到”“无析钠/无枝晶”“提高首圈库仑效率”
   “该添加剂抑制产气”）不得写成 `mechanism_keyword` 关键词表——关键词命中分不清
   “发生腐蚀”与“未发生腐蚀”。改用 `kind: "evidence_claim"`：在 `claim` 里用一句
   用户原话写出对单个候选须成立的断言，在 `claim_verdicts` 里**逐候选**给出判定。
   语义判断（这段原文是否为该候选建立或推翻该断言）由你负责；程序只做两件可机械
   核验的事：判定须指向本次请求的候选，`quote` 须在该候选证据正文中逐字存在。
   因此措辞、否定、同义称呼的变化都不影响判定，你只需如实读原文：
   - `supported`：有原文明确为该候选建立断言，附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `refuted`：有原文明确反驳（如原文说“会持续腐蚀铝箔”），附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `not_found`：检索到的证据未直接提及，如实填写，由补证机制驱动下一轮检索。
   背景介绍、他人体系的结果、无实验支撑的预测都不算 `supported`。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "constraint_id": "no-corrosion",
     "description": "no current-collector or case corrosion observed",
     "kind": "evidence_claim",
     "claim": "该候选电解液不腐蚀铝箔或钢壳",
     "claim_verdicts": [
       {
         "candidate_id": "candidate-1",
         "verdict": "refuted",
         "chunk_id": "fan2024::sec3",
         "quote": "the single NaFSI system can continuously corrode aluminum foil and stainless steel sheets",
         "basis": "原文明确说明单盐 NaFSI 会持续腐蚀铝箔与不锈钢，与该断言相反。"
       }
     ],
     "can_replan": true,
     "search_hint": "find corrosion test evidence for the candidate electrolyte"
   }
   ```
   `evidence_claim` 不得把 `required_evidence_scope` 设为 `component` 或 `background`：
   断言必须由候选自身绑定的证据支持，不能借用别篇论文或背景段落的措辞。
   给出 `supported` 前，逐句核对引文是否真正支持所写断言。引文必须从指定
   `chunk_id` 返回的原文复制，不能把题名、摘要或另一块文字放在该块的标识下。
   配方、测试条件和性能必须对应同一候选；一种优点不能替代另一项目标的证据。
   成本动机与价格比较分别表述，安全性或无氟组成不能自行推导出成本优势。
   `basis` 说明原句与断言的推理关系，不得以重复断言代替理由。程序核验引文
   存在及归属，不代替科学含义判断；证据未支持完整断言时应补证或保留 `not_found`。
   `criteria`/`target_conditions` 仅用于兼容旧调用方；新设计任务必须优先使用
   `constraint_records`，避免 evaluator 再从自由文本猜测硬约束。

   `required_evidence_kinds` 描述的是**支持记录本身的语义角色**，不是实验条件元数据。
   数值性能约束通常只要求 `property`；温度、电极、循环数等共同实例化条件应由该
   observation 的 `condition_scope` 和 `joint_context_requirements` 表达。除非硬约束本身
   确实要求一条独立的 condition 记录，否则不要把同一数值约束写成
   `required_evidence_kinds=["property", "condition"]`，否则会把“带条件上下文的性能观测”
   错当成缺少第二种证据角色。

   当两个及以上硬约束必须在**同一个目标实验上下文**中同时成立时，还必须显式写
   `joint_context_requirements`。分别在多个倍率测试的要求，按倍率分别建立条件组，
   每组的 `target_context.rate` 只填一个倍率。不能把 `0.5 C and 1 C` 当成一次测试的倍率。
   同一论文的不同盐浓度或溶剂比例必须分别对应其性能段，不能因来自同篇论文就互换结果。
   `target_context.cell_configuration` 使用条件检查器的外形名称 `pouch` 或 `coin`，
   不拼成 `pouch full cell` 这样的新标签。全电池要求另用 cell_configuration 检查条件
   和明确的正负极对验证；外形名称不能代替电极与全电池要求。
   它描述的是 evidence composition obligation，不要求所有
   支持证据拥有相同 `experiment_id`。`constraint_ids` 只能引用本次 `constraint_records`；
   `context_fields` 只列对联合决策真正相关的字段；`target_context` 只填写用户明确给出的
   目标条件，未知字段保持未知，禁止为了让 join 成立而补默认值。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "joint_context_requirements": [
       {
         "group_id": "low-temp-high-voltage",
         "constraint_ids": ["retention", "voltage"],
         "context_fields": ["temperature_c", "electrode"],
         "target_context": {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"},
         "can_replan": true,
         "search_hint": "find evidence satisfying both hard constraints at the target operating context"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
   只有约束确实需要共同实例化时才声明 joint group；互不相关的硬约束不要强行合组。
   原文条件检查器分别识别 `electrode` 与 `cell_configuration`。涉及电池形式的用户要求
   使用独立的 cell_configuration 条件；只有相关观测明确提供该字段时，才作联合检查。
2. 检查用户输入与已有 ledger；存在组分、机理或替代体系缺口时，选择相应检索能力；
3. 如证据不足，再做有界补充检索：
   - 区分“已有候选缺少一段证据”和“已有候选并不适合目标”。先检查最相关论文；
     若当前候选仍不能满足目标，按缺口与完整目标检索其他候选，不反复只查原来的
     盐、溶剂或论文。新证据支持新的组成时重新组装候选，再用原任务的全部条件
     筛选。不能把不同候选的成本、工况或性能拼成一个通过的候选。
   - 尚未定位候选论文时，用 `search_literature_chunks` 做 1–2 次聚焦补充（`top_k=10`）；
   - 若返回结果已经给出明确 `paper_id`，且该论文与目标组分/机理直接相关但缺少显式配方或目标工况证据，必须对最相关的 1 篇论文调用一次 `search_paper_chunks(paper_id=..., query=..., top_k=8)`；`query` 用 4–8 个英文技术词描述缺失事实，不含作者名。将结果追加到 `evidence_chunks`，不得跨论文拼接配方与性能。
   - 对 **named-study / named-candidate** 设计任务，在进入 `query_formulation_space` 或
     `screen_formulations` 前，必须先取得同一论文中可追溯的配方/组成证据：至少有一条
     `evidence_kind="formulation"` 的记录能支持候选的盐、溶剂或添加剂组成。只有性能、温度、
     机理 chunk 不能建立候选配方归属；若当前只找到性能证据，应继续检索 formulation /
     composition 段落，而不是手工构造一个 `formulation_evidence_ids=[]` 的候选进入筛选。
4. 用户没有提供可评估候选时，调用 `query_formulation_space`，把目标转成：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","target_conditions":[...],"preferred_salts":[...],"preferred_solvents":[...],"preferred_additives":[...],"excluded_components":[...],"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"max_candidates":3}}`；其中 `evidence_chunks` 必须传入前面检索实际返回、与目标最相关的最多 12 个 chunk，不得只传组分偏好而丢失文献上下文。工具会优先从这些同论文原文块组装候选，再使用 KG fallback；保留工具原样返回的 `candidates`。
   如果候选 evidence 只有 `chunk_id` 而 `text/excerpt` 为空，先调用
   `enrich_formulation_evidence({"request":{"candidates": candidates}})`，并用返回候选
   替换原列表；证据已有原文时不得为形式完整重复调用。enrichment 只补齐原文和元数据，
   必须保留原 evidence 的 `paper_id`、`evidence_kind` 和 `chunk_id`。
5. 若任务涉及离子电导率、温度下的传输性质或需要在多个 NaPF6–EC/EMC/PC 候选之间增加一个轻量定量参考，可在筛选前调用 `predict_formulation_conductivity`。只有以下两种情况允许数值预测：候选已有明确的 NaPF6/EC/EMC/PC 摩尔组成，或调用参数中的 `composition_inputs[candidate_id]` 显式给出 `component_mmol`、`molar_ratios` 或 `x_NaSalt/x_EC/x_PC`。现有 `solvent_ratios` 没有保存 v/v、w/w 或 molar 基准，因此**不得**仅凭“1 M + 1:1”之类字段推导模型输入。含其他盐、其他溶剂或添加剂的候选按域外处理；组成不足时保留 `insufficient_composition`，继续依赖文献/KG 证据。`model_predictions` 与 literature evidence 必须分开：模型预测可以辅助候选比较和后续实验优先级，但不能单独把实验事实型硬约束判为满足。
6. 只有需要形成配方推荐或明确 hold 时才调用 `screen_formulations`：
   传入当前候选和完整的结构化 `constraint_records`。旧文本字段用于兼容历史输入，
   新设计任务不能用它们替代结构化条件。
   每项 `claim_verdicts` 只判定本次 `candidates` 中实际提交的候选。候选集合变更时，
   同步更新各断言的候选判定，保持原任务的全部条件。工具返回参数错误后，修复
   指出的字段并重新提交完整请求，不得删去 `constraint_records` 或联合条件来消除报错。
    倍率与循环次数是两种不同测试，分别建立约束：指定 1 C 测试使用
    `{"kind":"c_rate","operator":"==","value":1,"unit":"C"}`；
    100 次循环使用 `{"kind":"minimum_cycles","value":100,"unit":"cycles"}`。
    指定 2.0–4.0 V 测试使用
    `{"kind":"voltage_window","operator":"==","value":[2.0,4.0],"unit":"V"}`。
    若任务要求 0.5 C 和 1 C，各自建立条件。
    双盐配方同时保存 `salts` 与 `salt_concentrations_mol_l`，分别记录各盐浓度；
    `concentration_mol_l` 表示总盐浓度，不得将它归给某一个盐。
    `solvent_ratio_basis` 按原文填写 `mass`、`volume` 或 `molar`；原文未说明时填
    `unknown`。不得把质量比例当成体积比例，或把溶剂比例直接当成包括盐的摩尔组成。
   若本任务已声明 `joint_context_requirements`，每次首次筛选和补证后的重新筛选都必须携带
   同一份 joint-context 合同；除非用户明确修改任务目标，否则不得在 re-screen 时删除、
   放宽 `context_fields` 或改写 `target_context`。runtime 会在字段被意外省略时保留上一版
   显式合同，但 Agent 仍应主动原样传递。
   保留工具原样返回的 `screening_results`、其中的 `criteria_evaluations` 与 `gaps`，
   不得手写分数、validations 或 scores。任何 `failed`、`insufficient_evidence` 或
   `unsupported` 判定都不得在报告中表述为性能已验证。
7. 旧调用方需要动作列表时，可调用 `optimize_formulations`：
   `{"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results,"request":{"task_type":"design","objectives":[目标性能...],"constraints":[用户硬约束...]}}`。
   不得同时传入 `validations` 或 `scores`。该兼容工具只翻译筛选后已经产生的
   `DecisionState`，不会再按 score 独立裁决；若 proposal 为
   `retrieve_more_evidence`，先执行对应的补充检索和重新筛选，再进入报告。
8. `DecisionState` 已达到 `recommend` 或 `hold` 后，必须**立即**调用 `synthesize_design_report`
   生成完整报告，并传入同一份原始 `screening_results`：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","question":用户问题,"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results}}`。
   为提升 `claim_supported_ratio`，请在 `request.claims` 中提交**所有**被 `evidence_chunks` 直接支持的事实声明（`claim_type="fact"`），每条包含 `text`、对应 `chunk_id` 和唯一逐字原文引文 `evidence_quote`（必须从该 chunk 的 `content` 中逐字截取，且只出现一次）。**禁止为凑数量编造 claim**；若当前证据能直接支持的 claim 不足 2 条，应优先通过 `search_literature_chunks` 或 `search_paper_chunks` 补充检索，最多尝试 2 轮；若仍无法找到更多直接支持，则在报告中明确标注“证据不足”，并只提交已被验证的 claim。报告将渲染“已校验事实”小节，避免裁判从自由文本中抽取不被检索上下文支持的论断。
   报告要让使用者能安排下一步工作。用简明中文分别提交配方组成、文献的测试条件与数值、同条件基准配方的结果，并保留逐字引文。比例需说明质量比或体积比；浓度、添加剂用量不得省略或猜测。文献筛选不能写成新配方已由本智能体实验验证。
   当目标是某项性能时，报告必须包含已检索到的该项性能结果，不能只列出温度、
   电极和电压范围等测试设置。不同盐浓度、溶剂比例和添加剂分支的结果分别绑定到
   其配方。不得借用另一分支较好的结果；保留同一分支完整组成与性能已明确的候选，
   不必强求选取数值最高但组成仍缺失的分支。
   `next_steps` 按本次缺口列出具体核查或实验，包括要比较的配方、温度、倍率、电池类型和测量项目；这些是验证计划，不是已取得的结果。即使为 `hold`，也要展示已取得的候选资料、文献结果和暂缓原因，不得只写状态或检索流程。
   对没有数值判据的选材目标，`next_steps` 也要交代其验证状态。例如成本目标
   需要区分文献的成本动机与实际价格比较，不能因筛选通过就宣称全部目标已验证。
   性能类 `claims` 应优先包含与当前候选直接相连的实验结果，少选一般背景介绍。

9. 直接输出报告全文，不得改写或截断。

## 退出纪律

- 不要求无条件调用所有工具；根据用户已有候选和结构化 evidence gaps 选择能力。
- `synthesize_design_report` 是终端编译能力。调用前必须已有终态 `DecisionState`；
  `search` 状态必须先按缺口补证或换候选，不能用固定工具次数代替状态判断。
- `recommend` 只推荐 approved candidates；`hold` 展示已检索的候选资料与文献结果，说明缺口和验证计划，不推荐或排序候选。

## 候选方案纪律

- 候选配方必须来自 KG 结构化证据或文献 chunk；
- 对于"建议组合"（无完整配方直接实验数据），summary 只写组分和证据来源，不写性能声明；
- 性能/效果声明只能绑定到直接支持该声明的 chunk_id；
- 禁止在"证据摘要"里写入未被任何 chunk 直接支持的推断句；无来源支撑的直接删除；
- **直接回答（direct_answer）只给出候选方案标识和最精简组成**，不要包含"已在某温度验证"、"性能最优"、"最有效"等需要跨证据推断的断言；
- 推荐完整配方必须有原文明确的钠盐浓度。若浓度未知，列为待补资料，不得填入
  “参考基准配方”的浓度并作为已有文献验证的配方推荐。

## 推荐/排序纪律

- 排序理由必须逐条绑定到具体 chunk_id，禁止写"C1/C3/C4 无法满足需求"、"某候选明显优于其他"等无直接对比证据的绝对化断言；
- 无直接对比证据时，只陈述各候选的组分、证据来源与评分，不给出相对优劣结论；
- 对"建议组合"的推荐，只能说明其组分和所依据的证据，不得把多篇证据的性能迁移到该组合上。

## 证据摘要纪律

- 配方段落若讨论多种浓度、多个溶剂比例或不同研究，先定位到单一配方的原文。
  不得把某段的浓度、另一配方的溶剂比例和第三个体系的添加剂拼成候选。
  原文工具返回中的数值、温度符号、配方标识和 chunk_id 应原样沿用，
  不得手工改写成另一温度或用整篇论文的共同身份代替相同测试条件。
- 每条 bullet 必须附带 `[chunk_id]`；
- 禁止输出以"【推断】"开头的句子；
- 禁止把多篇证据的性能迁移到某个候选配方上。

## 引用纪律

- 使用 `[chunk_id]` 格式；
- 禁止引用模型参数知识里的文献；
- 单篇报道就写"某文献报道/某体系显示"，不得升格为普适结论。

## KG 质量反馈

检索或分析过程中，若发现以下可疑情况，**必须**调用 `flag_suspicious_kg_item` 记录，供后续离线人工审查与 KG 矫正；不阻塞当前设计流程。

- **实体标签错误**：如 `ionic conductivity` 被标为 `Additive`，`NaPF6` 被标为 `Solvent`；
- **关系方向/语义错误**：如 `SEI DECOMPOSITION::FORMS::FEC`、明显违背化学常识的关系；
- **属性单位或数值异常**：如电导率 `100 mS/cm` 与上下文矛盾、温度单位混用；
- **同名异义**：如 `TMP` 同时指 `trimethyl phosphate` 与 `2,4,6-trimethylpyridine` 而未区分；
- **证据与 KG 矛盾**：chunk 中的明确结论与 KG 检索结果冲突。

记录时尽量提供：item_type（`entity`/`relation`/`property`）、具体名称/ID、问题描述、触发工具、证据 chunk_id。

## 知识沉淀

设计流程全部结束后，调用 `reflect_now` 进行知识反思和 Wiki 沉淀，
将本次设计的关键结论、发现的知识缺口、改进的检索关键词记录到 LLM Wiki，
供下次相似问题时直接检索复用，减少重复检索成本。

Abstract Hard carbon (HC) remains the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its low initial Coulombic efficiency and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) hinder long-term performance. Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Here we propose a “revitalization” strategy to clarify the synergistic influence of solvent and anion chemistry by systematically evaluating three electrolytes: 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in diethylene glycol dimethyl ether ( $NaPF_{6}-G2$ ), and 1.0 M sodium trifluoromethanesulfonate in G2 (NaOTF-G2). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . The HC samples using three comparison electrolytes of $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ , $NaPF_{6}-G2$ , and NaOTF-G2 electrolytes were prepared and tested in coin-type half-cells. To detect the effect of the anionic group and solvent for a detailed understanding of sodium storage behavior in HC, cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements and galvanostatic discharge/charge (GCD) tests were carried out. During the first discharge process, HC using three electrolytes all show a wide band at 0.15–1.0 V, representing the spontaneous interaction of $Na^{+}$ with defects and SEI formation (Figure S1a, Supporting Information online) [29]. evidence_chunks.content: To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP ||HC was examined at 10 mA g-1 and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP ||HC pouch cell under a low temperature of -40 °C still exhibits a high specific capacity of 42.7 mAh g-1 even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec8::child0
evidence_chunks.content: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M NaPF6-EC/DMC, 1.0 M NaPF6-G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on Na+ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec7
evidence_chunks.content: Temperature-dependent conductivity and viscosity measurements reveal that NaOTF-G2 exhibits superior low-temperature performance compared to NaPF6-EC/DMC and NaPF6-G2 (Figure S15). While NaPF6-EC/DMC shows higher conductivity above -20°C due to its low viscosity, it solidifies upon cooling, leading to a sharp decline in ionic mobility. In contrast, NaOTF-G2 maintains a conductivity of 1.02 mS cm-1 at -40°C, attributed to weak Na+-OTF- coordination and favorable solvation dynamics that suppress salt aggregation and freezing. Further, the cycling performance of HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte was investigated at low temperatures and 50 mA g-1, as depicted in Figure 5B. During the first cycle, HC maintains a high discharge specific capacity of 159.7 mAh g-1 at a low temperature of -40°C. After 100 cycles, an excellent capacity retention of 78.5% can still be achieved.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child1
evidence_chunks.content: To test the practical application of electrolytes, a piece pouch cell (45 mAh) was assembled for cycling testing in Figure 6d and Figure S26 (Supporting Information). After cycling 100 cycles at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 86.7%. Then, the pouch cell was cycled 100 cycles at -30 °C, and the capacity retention rate was 92.43% in Figure 6e.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec5::child0
evidence_chunks.content: To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. Additionally, the performance of the full cell was evaluated at -40 °C and it was manifested that the full cell using 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL can preserve 64.8% of its capacity at 25 °C in Figure 6b. After 50 cycles of 0.1 C (10 mA g-1) at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 95.7%, and then after 50 cycles of 0.1 C at -40 °C, the capacity retention rate was 92.8%, as shown in Figure 6c.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec6::child3
evidence_chunks.content: At low temperatures of -20 and -40 °C, the NTM-based electrolyte still delivers high discharge capacities of 71.5 mA h g-1 and 62.2 mA h g-1, corresponding to 83.2% and 72.4% of the discharge capacity at room temperature, respectively (Figure 5g). Additionally, the battery can stably complete 50 discharge cycles at -20 °C (Figure S43, Supporting Information), and even successfully operate for 20 cycles at -40 °C, maintaining a capacity retention rate of 83.9% (Figure 5h; Figure S44, Supporting Information).

evidence_chunks.content: When the temperature drops to -40 °C, as shown in Fig. 3(e), the MP-based electrolyte remains 96% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 0.1 C.

evidence.text: Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak Na+-G2 interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of OTF--anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of ~200 mAh g-1 over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a Na3V2(PO4)3||HC pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at -40 °C.

evidence.paper_title: 0046_Luo 2026 Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes
evidence.text: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M NaPF6-EC/DMC, 1.0 M NaPF6-G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on Na+ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between Na+ and G2 allows more anions to enter the Na+ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high Na+ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF--anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles.

evidence.section_title: 2.5 Na storage properties at ultralow temperatures
evidence.text: To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP ||HC was examined at 10 mA g-1 and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP ||HC pouch cell under a low temperature of -40 °C still exhibits a high specific capacity of 42.7 mAh g-1 even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity. Furthermore, no obvious enhancement in polarization during charging and discharging is observed, indicating stable interphases and no obvious side reactions in the NVP ||HC pouch cells using 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte.

evidence.section_title: 2.5 Na storage properties at ultralow temperatures
evidence.text: With decreasing temperature, batteries experience significantly increased interfacial impedance and pronounced capacity decay, closely linked to the desolvation and migration of Na+ through the SEI. Temperature-dependent conductivity and viscosity measurements reveal that NaOTF-G2 exhibits superior low-temperature performance compared to NaPF6-EC/DMC and NaPF6-G2 (Figure S15). While NaPF6-EC/DMC shows higher conductivity above -20°C due to its low viscosity, it solidifies upon cooling, leading to a sharp decline in ionic mobility. In contrast, NaOTF-G2 maintains a conductivity of 1.02 mS cm-1 at -40°C, attributed to weak Na+-OTF- coordination and favorable solvation dynamics that suppress salt aggregation and freezing. These properties ensure sustained ion transport and stable interfacial chemistry even under extreme cold conditions. Thanks to the low-solvation electrolytes and homogeneous SEI, the NaOTF-G2 system achieves competitive performance even at the extremely low temperature of -40°C (Figure 5A). Further, the cycling performance of HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte was investigated at low temperatures and 50 mA g-1, as depicted in Figure 5B. During the first cycle, HC maintains a high discharge specific capacity of 159.7 mAh g-1 at a low temperature of -40°C. After 100 cycles, an excellent capacity retention of 78.5% can still be achieved.
