evidence.paper_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries
evidence.section_title: 2.1. The Solvation Structure at RT and Physical Properties
evidence.text: Primarily, Na+-O (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to Na+-O (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, Na+ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes Na+ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point (-95 °C) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

evidence.text: To test the practical application of electrolytes, a piece pouch cell (45 mAh) was assembled for cycling testing in Figure 6d and Figure S26 (Supporting Information). After cycling 100 cycles at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 86.7%. Then, the pouch cell was cycled 100 cycles at -30 °C, and the capacity retention rate was 92.43% in Figure 6e. Therefore, 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL electrolyte with a temperature-adaptive solvent structure holds great potential in the practical application of SIBs.

evidence.text: To further verify the feasibility of electrolytes in SIBs, the coin full cell with NVP cathode and pre-cycled HC anode was assembled and subjected to rate performance testing at 25 °C. It displays that the full cell coupled with 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL can still retain a capacity of 71.6 mAh g-1 at 10 C, while the cell using 0.5 M NaPF6 G2 can only bestow a capacity of 52.3 mAh g-1 in Figure 6a. Additionally, the performance of the full cell was evaluated at -40 °C and it was manifested that the full cell using 0.5 M NaPF6 G2/DOL can preserve 64.8% of its capacity at 25 °C in Figure 6b. After 50 cycles of 0.1 C (10 mA g-1) at 25 °C, the capacity retention rate was 95.7%, and then after 50 cycles of 0.1 C at -40 °C, the capacity retention rate was 92.8%, as shown in Figure 6c.

evidence.text: Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups.

evidence.paper_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery
evidence.text: In addition, the NVP||HC full cell employing the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 100 cycles under the extreme conditions of high voltage (4.3 V) and 50 °C (Figure S42, Supporting Information). The NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte exhibits remarkable temperature adaptability across a broad temperature range. At low temperatures of -20 and -40 °C, the NTM-based electrolyte still delivers high discharge capacities of 71.5 mA h g-1 and 62.2 mA h g-1, corresponding to 83.2% and 72.4% of the discharge capacity at room temperature, respectively (Figure 5g). Additionally, the battery can stably complete 50 discharge cycles at -20 °C (Figure S43, Supporting Information), and even successfully operate for 20 cycles at -40 °C, maintaining a capacity retention rate of 83.9% (Figure 5h; Figure S44, Supporting Information).

evidence.text: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g-1 and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g-1, maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c.

claim_verdicts.quote: Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles.
claim_verdicts.basis: 同一段原文同时给出 -40 °C、100 次循环、NVP||HC 软包电芯与约 81% 的容量保持率，正是用户要求的工况与观测量。

-40 °C 下仅报告 20 个循环（83.9%）；100 循环数据在 50 °C 与室温下取得，且未报告软包电芯。
-40 °C 的 100 循环 96% 保持率来自 Na||NVPOF 半电池，正极为 NVPOF 而非 NVP，也没有软包电芯。
该记录来自电解液综述表格，与 -40 °C、HC||NVP 软包电芯无任何同实验绑定证据。

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec1::child1
evidence_chunks.content: Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . This work provides molecular-level insights into electrolyte design principles and highlights the critical role of solvation structure in enabling durable low-temperature sodium storage. Keywords sodium-ion battery, solvation chemistry, solvent, salt anion, SEI components

evidence_chunks.content: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. ## 配方筛选结果 已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。 ### 候选资料：luo2026-naotf-g2（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaOTF；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaOTF：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：diglyme (G2, diethylene glycol dimethyl ether)。 - 配方原文 [0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec1::child1]：Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . This work provides molecular-level insights into electrolyte design principles and highlights the critical role of solvation structure in enabling durable low-temperature sodium storage. Keywords sodium-ion battery, solvation chemistry, solvent, salt anion, SEI components ### 候选资料：cui2025-napf6-g2dol（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：diglyme (G2, diethylene glycol dimethyl ether), 1,3-dioxolane (DOL)；溶剂比例（体积）：diglyme (G2)=3, 1,3-dioxolane (DOL)=1。 - 配方原文 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]：Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed. ### 候选资料：chang2025-ntm（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：triethyl phosphate (TEP), methyl propionate (MP)；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=6, MP=4；添加剂：vinylene carbonate (VC)；添加剂用量：vinylene carbonate (VC)=1 wt%。 - 配方原文 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2]：The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information). ### 候选资料：liu2024-napf6-mp-fec（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：methyl propionate (MP), fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)；溶剂比例（体积）：methyl propionate (MP)=9, fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)=1；添加剂：fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)；添加剂用量：fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)=10 vol% (9:1 vol)。 - 配方原文 [0038_Liu 等 - 2024 - Ester-based anti-freezing electrolyte achieving ultra-low temperature cycling for sodium-ion batteri::sec6::child0]：The electrolyte is prepared in an argon-filled glove box, where the water and oxygen contents are both less than 0.1 ppm. The electrolyte we designed for this work is 2 M NaPF $_{6}$ (DoDoChem, >99.8%) dissolved in methyl propionate (MP, >99%, Macklin) and FEC (DoDoChem, >99.9%) at 9:1 (vol.%). The control electrolyte is 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ dissolved in PC (Sigma Aldrich, >99%) and FEC at 9:1 (vol.%). ### 候选资料：same-paper-1（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaTi2(PO4)3；溶剂：PYR14TFSI, PC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：PYR14TFSI=0.5, PC=0.5。 - 配方原文 [0114_0097_Electrolytes_for_electrochemical_energy::sec19::child4]：Materials Chemistry Frontiers

2.5 Na storage properties at ultralow temperatures
With decreasing temperature, batteries experience significantly increased interfacial impedance and pronounced capacity decay, closely linked to the desolvation and migration of $Na^{+}$ through the SEI [50,51]. Therefore, achieving excellent Na storage properties at subzero temperatures hinges on minimizing the desolvation energy of $Na^{+}$ [52]. Temperature-dependent conductivity and viscosity measurements reveal that NaOTF-G2 exhibits superior low-temperature performance compared to $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ and $NaPF_{6}-G2$ (Figure S15). While $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ shows higher conductivity above $-20^{\circ}C$ due to its low viscosity, it solidifies upon cooling, leading to a sharp decline in ionic mobility. In contrast, NaOTF-G2 maintains a conductivity of $1.02\ mS\ cm^{-1}$ at $-40^{\circ}C$ , attributed to weak $Na^{+}-OTF^{-}$ coordination and favorable solvation dynamics that suppress salt aggregation and freezing. These properties ensure sustained ion transport and stable interfacial chemistry even under extreme cold conditions. Thanks to the low-solvation electrolytes and homogeneous SEI, the NaOTF-G2 system achieves competitive performance even at the extremely low temperature of $-40^{\circ}C$ (Figure 5A). Although electrochemical tests were conducted at $-40^{\circ}C$ , theoretical calculations were performed at $-30^{\circ}C$ to ensure computational stability. This temperature still represents a relevant low-temperature regime and provides meaningful insight consistent with the experimental results. Further, the cycling performance of HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte was investigated at low temperatures and $50\ mA\ g^{-1}$ , as depicted in Figure 5B. During the first cycle, HC maintains a high discharge specific capacity of $159.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}C$ . After 100 cycles, an excellent capacity retention of 78.5% can still be achieved. The charge/discharge curves of the HC after the second cycle show a good overlap, indicating stability in specific capacity and high reversibility during electrochemical reactions (Figure 5C). Besides, the SEI formed in NaOTF-G2 exhibits a distinct composition enriched with fluorinated organic species ( $SO_{2}F^{-}, CF_{3}SO_{3}^{-}$ ) and inner $NaS_{x}$ layers at $-40^{\circ}C$ , differing from room-temperature NaF-dominated SEI, and contr

Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

Received 9 May 2025; Accepted 11 August 2025; Published online 16 October 2025

Abstract Hard carbon (HC) remains the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its low initial Coulombic efficiency and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) hinder long-term performance. Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Here we propose a “revitalization” strategy to clarify the synergistic influence of solvent and anion chemistry by systematically evaluating three electrolytes: 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in diethylene glycol dimethyl ether ( $NaPF_{6}-G2$ ), and 1.0 M sodium trifluoromethanesulfonate in G2 (NaOTF-G2). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . citations.chunk_id: 0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec8::child0
citations.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

citations.quote: Figure S18 presents the longer cycling performance of $MoS_{2}$ , conducted to further confirm the extended durability and stability of the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. More importantly, $MoS_{2}$ cycled at $0.5\;A\;g^{-1}$ in the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte maintains a high reversible specific capacity of $60.6\;mAh\;g^{-1}$ even after 300 cycles, with an average CE reaching 99.7%. To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ was examined at $10\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell under a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ still exhibits a high specific capacity of $42.7\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity. Furthermore, no obvious enhancement in polarization during charging and discharging is observed, indicating stable interphases and no obvious side reactions in the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cells using 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. Figure 5I illustrates the $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ -solvates interfacial behaviors in the optimized 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, showing reduced desolvation energy and enhanced transfer kinetics across a broad temperature range.

citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

association_citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

citations.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

With decreasing temperature, batteries experience significantly increased interfacial impedance and pronounced capacity decay, closely linked to the desolvation and migration of $Na^{+}$ through the SEI [50,51]. Therefore, achieving excellent Na storage properties at subzero temperatures hinges on minimizing the desolvation energy of $Na^{+}$ [52]. Temperature-dependent conductivity and viscosity measurements reveal that NaOTF-G2 exhibits superior low-temperature performance compared to $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ and $NaPF_{6}-G2$ (Figure S15). While $NaPF_{6}-EC/DMC$ shows higher conductivity above $-20^{\circ}C$ due to its low viscosity, it solidifies upon cooling, leading to a sharp decline in ionic mobility. In contrast, NaOTF-G2 maintains a conductivity of $1.02\ mS\ cm^{-1}$ at $-40^{\circ}C$ , attributed to weak $Na^{+}-OTF^{-}$ coordination and favorable solvation dynamics that suppress salt aggregation and freezing. These properties ensure sustained ion transport and stable interfacial chemistry even under extreme cold conditions. Thanks to the low-solvation electrolytes and homogeneous SEI, the NaOTF-G2 system achieves competitive performance even at the extremely low temperature of $-40^{\circ}C$ (Figure 5A). Although electrochemical tests were conducted at $-40^{\circ}C$ , theoretical calculations were performed at $-30^{\circ}C$ to ensure computational stability. This temperature still represents a relevant low-temperature regime and provides meaningful insight consistent with the experimental results. Further, the cycling performance of HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte was investigated at low temperatures and $50\ mA\ g^{-1}$ , as depicted in Figure 5B. During the first cycle, HC maintains a high discharge specific capacity of $159.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}C$ . Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

Sainan Luo $^{1}$ , Zhen Hou $^{1}$ , Zixin Qi $^{1}$ , Qin Li $^{3}$ , Yuepeng Pang $^{1}$ , Jiafeng Ruan $^{2,3*}$ & Shiyou Zheng $^{1,4*}$

Received 9 May 2025; Accepted 11 August 2025; Published online 16 October 2025

Abstract Hard carbon (HC) remains the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its low initial Coulombic efficiency and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) hinder long-term performance. Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Here we propose a “revitalization” strategy to clarify the synergistic influence of solvent and anion chemistry by systematically evaluating three electrolytes: 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in diethylene glycol dimethyl ether ( $NaPF_{6}-G2$ ), and 1.0 M sodium trifluoromethanesulfonate in G2 (NaOTF-G2). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . citations.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

citations.quote: Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . This work provides molecular-level insights into electrolyte design principles and highlights the critical role of solvation structure in enabling durable low-temperature sodium storage. Keywords sodium-ion battery, solvation chemistry, solvent, salt anion, SEI components

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.chunk_id: 0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2
citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

citations.quote: Furthermore, the NTM electrolyte enables excellent rate performance at 50 °C and even stable cycling at an extreme temperature of 80 °C (Figures S25 and S26, Supporting Information). This superior performance is attributed to the formation of a robust NaF-enriched interface and thermally stable TEP. association_citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

citations.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

association_citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

Received 9 May 2025; Accepted 11 August 2025; Published online 16 October 2025

Abstract Hard carbon (HC) remains the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its low initial Coulombic efficiency and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) hinder long-term performance. Electrolyte engineering offers a promising strategy to regulate SEI chemistry, enhancing interfacial $Na^{+}$ transport and interphase stability. However, the respective roles of solvents and anions in tailoring the SEI on HC remain elusive. Here we propose a “revitalization” strategy to clarify the synergistic influence of solvent and anion chemistry by systematically evaluating three electrolytes: 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ in diethylene glycol dimethyl ether ( $NaPF_{6}-G2$ ), and 1.0 M sodium trifluoromethanesulfonate in G2 (NaOTF-G2). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . citations.quote: In summary, a series of electrolytes (1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -EC/DMC, 1.0 M $NaPF_{6}$ -G2, and 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolytes) was chosen in this study to investigate the separate effects of salt and solvent on $Na^{+}$ storage mechanisms in hard carbon anodes at a wide range of temperatures. The weak interaction between $Na^{+}$ and G2 allows more anions to enter the $Na^{+}$ solvation shell and forms the anion-derived robust and inorganic-rich interphase. This interface satisfies ion conductivity and facilitates a high $Na^{+}$ transference number, with superior redox kinetics in ether-based solvents, leading to excellent rate performance. Moreover, the preferential decomposition of OTF $^{-}$ -anions induces a highly uniform and ultrahigh inorganic-rich SEI, inhibiting side reactions and enhancing ICE as well as extending cycle lifespan. The HC using NaOTF-G2 electrolyte delivers an ideal ICE of 89.8% and achieves a specific capacity of 283.0 mAh g $^{-1}$ after 100 cycles. Even at -40 °C, the NVP | | HC full pouch cell still maintains approximately 81% of its excellent specific capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel and universal electrolyte design strategy to optimize the electrochemical behavior of electrode materials by targeting the roles of solvents and anions.

More importantly, $MoS_{2}$ cycled at $0.5\;A\;g^{-1}$ in the NaOTF-G2 electrolyte maintains a high reversible specific capacity of $60.6\;mAh\;g^{-1}$ even after 300 cycles, with an average CE reaching 99.7%. To further demonstrate the practical application of the 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, a pouch cell was assembled using an NVP cathode and an HC anode. The cyclic stability of the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ was examined at $10\mathrm{mA}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and low temperature, as shown in Figure 5G, H. The NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell under a low temperature of $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ still exhibits a high specific capacity of $42.7\mathrm{mAh}\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ even after 100 cycles. Figure 5H shows the corresponding GCD curves at different cycles. The GCD curves in the voltage window of 1.5–3.8 V show good reversibility except for a small attenuation of capacity. Furthermore, no obvious enhancement in polarization during charging and discharging is observed, indicating stable interphases and no obvious side reactions in the NVP $||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cells using 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte. Figure 5I illustrates the $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ -solvates interfacial behaviors in the optimized 1.0 M NaOTF-G2 electrolyte, showing reduced desolvation energy and enhanced transfer kinetics across a broad temperature range.

Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . This work provides molecular-level insights into electrolyte design principles and highlights the critical role of solvation structure in enabling durable low-temperature sodium storage. Keywords sodium-ion battery, solvation chemistry, solvent, salt anion, SEI components

citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec6::child0
citations.quote: In summary, we present a low-temperature adaptive electrolyte that is compatible with high $Na^{+}$ desolvation rates for SIBs by regulating solvation structure. Due to the weakened ion-dipole interaction of $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL has a low-temperature responsive solvation structure. As the temperature decreases, solvent coordination reduces and anion coordination increases in the first solvated shell of $Na^{+}$ . The temperature-sensitive solvation structure accelerates the desolvation of $Na^{+}$ , mitigating the voltage polarization on the HC surface. This enables HC to achieve higher capacity retention at high current density and low temperatures, thereby enhancing the low-temperature performance of SIBs. The HC anode realized a high capacity of 220.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ (1 C) at -40 °C, with 91.9% capacity retention after 900 cycles. At -30 °C, the capacity retention rate of HC||NVP pouch cell after 100 cycles at 0.1 C is 92.43%, indicating that electrolytes with low-temperature adaptation can effectively improve the low-temperature performance of SIBs. Noteworthy, temperature-adapted solvation structures universally exist in G2/DOL derivative electrolytes, which have exceedingly outstanding low-temperature performance. This provides a new way for designing low-temperature sodium-ion batteries and broadens their application for energy storage in extremely cold regions.

citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

citations.quote: To further validate the practicality of the NTM electrolyte, full cells with NVP cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes were constructed, operating within the voltage range of 2.0–3.6 V (Figure 5a). The NVP||HC full cell, without any presodiation treatment, exhibits a high specific capacity of 88.0 mA h g $^{-1}$ and excellent cycling stability over 100 cycles at 50 mA g $^{-1}$ , maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 84.9% in the NTM electrolyte. This retention markedly surpasses that of the conventional NP electrolyte (51.9%), as illustrated in Figure 5b,c. Furthermore, the full cell utilizing the NTM electrolyte demonstrates superior rate capability, delivering reversible capacities of 87.2, 82.0, 79.1, 77.0, 71.9, and 68.1 mA h g $^{-1}$ at 20, 50, 80, 100, 200, and 300 mA g $^{-1}$ , respectively (Figure 5d). The charge–discharge curves exhibit minimal polarization even at elevated rates (Figure S32, Supporting Information). In addition, the overall electrical performance of the NTM electrolyte is better than that of the NED (NP-EC/DMC) electrolyte (Figure S33, Supporting Information). Notably, the NVP||HC full cell with the NTM electrolyte maintains stable cycling for 500 cycles at a high current of 200 mA g $^{-1}$ (Figure S34, Supporting Information). Self-discharge behavior was further evaluated in the NVP||HC full-cell system. The results display that the NP electrolyte system retains 72.8% of its discharge capacity after 48 h of rest (based on 4th cycle).

association_citations.quote: The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

4. Conclusions
In summary, we designed a simple and efficient carboxylate ester-based electrolyte, using MP and FEC as the cosolvent in NVPOF instead of the most common PC-based electrolyte, which greatly enhances the low-temperature performance of the NVPOF cathode, mainly due to the enhanced ion conductivity and depressed electrode-electrolyte interface resistance. As a result, operating at $-25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF electrode with MP-based electrolyte can cycle for more than 500 cycles with a capacity of $82\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $1\mathrm{C}$ . Even at $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the NVPOF cathode still exhibits high-rate performance (50% capacity retention at $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ) and good cycling stability (96% capacity retention at $0.1\mathrm{C}$ after 100 cycles), reflecting the remarkable low-temperature performance of MP-based electrolyte. In addition, the low viscosity and freezing point of MP enable batteries to operate at temperatures as low as $-50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The homogeneous beneficial CEI formation and the fast kinetics of MP-based electrolytes at low temperatures were investigated by GITT and XPS tests, explaining the superiority of MP-based electrolytes as a low-temperature electrolyte compared to PC-based electrolytes. Additionally, the HC||NVPOF full cell has remarkable low-temperature performance as expected, delivering high initial discharge capacity of 108.4 and $73.0\mathrm{mAhg^{-1}}$ at $-25$ and $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , respectively. In short, the designed electrolyte enriches the SIBs applied in low temperatures, paving the way for further application of carboxylate ester-based electrolytes.

citations.quote: To solve the problem of sluggish ion mobility in the electrode materials at low temperatures, NASICON-type NVPOF with high intrinsic ion diffusion was selected as the cathode material to verify the availability of the designed MP-based electrolyte at sub-zero temperature operation. The preparation process, structure, and morphology characterization of the micron-size NVPOF were shown in the experimental section and Fig. S4, according to our previous work [42]. To confirm, the Na||NVPOF half-cells with different electrolytes were assembled to investigate the electrochemical performance at the temperature range from 25 to $-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in the voltage window of $2.5 - 4.3\mathrm{V}$ (vs. $\mathrm{Na^{+} / Na}$ ). At $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curves of the NVPOF electrode using two electrolytes are basically the same (Fig. 2(a)) except for the slight difference in the first coulombic efficiency, which means that the two electrolytes are well matched to the NVPOF cathode. And at $-25\ ^{\circ}C$ , the NVPOF half-cell with MP-based electrolyte delivers a specific capacity of $109.7\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C, equivalent to 91% of its specific capacity at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , higher than that of the PC-based electrolyte ( $102.3\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ ), moreover, the polarization of NVPOF electrode with PC-based electrolyte is obviously higher than that of the MP-based electrolyte, especially at the lower voltage plateau.

## 配方筛选结果 已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。 ### 候选资料：luo2026-naotf-g2（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaOTF；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaOTF：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：diglyme (G2, diethylene glycol dimethyl ether)。 - 配方原文 [0046_Luo 等 - 2026 - Insights into targeted effects of salt and solvent on Na storage in hard carbon anodes toward ultra::sec1::child1]：Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that weak $Na^{+}-G2$ interactions permit more anions to enter the primary solvation shell, facilitating the formation of an inorganic-rich SEI that promotes high ionic conductivity and redox kinetics. Additionally, the preferential decomposition of $OTF^{-}$ -anions results in a uniform and robust SEI. As a result, HC anodes cycled in NaOTF-G2 deliver a reversible specific capacity of $\sim200\ mAh\ g^{-1}$ over 3000 cycles. Furthermore, a $\mathrm{Na}_{3}\mathrm{V}_{2}(\mathrm{PO}_{4})_{3}||\mathrm{HC}$ pouch cell incorporating this optimized electrolyte achieves a capacity retention of 81% at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ . This work provides molecular-level insights into electrolyte design principles and highlights the critical role of solvation structure in enabling durable low-temperature sodium storage. Keywords sodium-ion battery, solvation chemistry, solvent, salt anion, SEI components ### 候选资料：cui2025-napf6-g2dol（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：diglyme (G2, diethylene glycol dimethyl ether), 1,3-dioxolane (DOL)；溶剂比例（体积）：diglyme (G2)=3, 1,3-dioxolane (DOL)=1。 - 配方原文 [0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0]：Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed. ### 候选资料：chang2025-ntm（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：triethyl phosphate (TEP), methyl propionate (MP)；溶剂比例（体积）：TEP=6, MP=4；添加剂：vinylene carbonate (VC)；添加剂用量：vinylene carbonate (VC)=1 wt%。 - 配方原文 [0004_Chang 等 - 2025 - Solvent-Fluorine-Free Anion-Enriched and Non-Flammable Electrolyte Enables Safe Sodium-Ion Battery::sec2::child2]：The Na+-MP complex exhibits a low binding energy (-1.38 eV), consistent with its low DN value, further validating the weak coordination ability of MP. The redox behavior of the electrolyte was further evaluated using molecular orbital theory (Figure S3, Supporting Information). PF6− possesses the lowest highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level (-10.16 eV), indicating strong resistance to electron loss and enhanced oxidative stability. Moreover, its low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) suggests preferential decomposition at the negative electrode, thereby improving interfacial compatibility with TEP. Based on optimizations in nonflammability, ionic conductivity and long cycle performance, the 2.0 M NaPF6 in TEP/MP +1 wt% VC (6:4 by volume ratio, denoted as NTM) is selected as the optimal electrolyte for further investigation (Figures S2 and S4, Supporting Information), with 2.0 M NaPF6 dissolved in TEP +1 wt% VC (denoted as NT) and traditional carbonate electrolyte 1.0 M NaPF6 in PC (denoted as NP) serving as control groups. Moreover, the NTM electrolyte not only exhibits a reduced contact angle with the separator (Figure S5, Supporting Information), indicative of decreased electrolyte viscosity and improved wettability, but also shows an oxidation potential of up to 4.52 V and a lower reduction potential (Figure S6, Supporting Information). ### 候选资料：liu2024-napf6-mp-fec（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：2 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：2 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：methyl propionate (MP), fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)；溶剂比例（体积）：methyl propionate (MP)=9, fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)=1；添加剂：fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)；添加剂用量：fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)=10 vol% (9:1 vol)。 - 配方原文 [0038_Liu 等 - 2024 - Ester-based anti-freezing electrolyte achieving ultra-low temperature cycling for sodium-ion batteri::sec6::child0]：The electrolyte is prepared in an argon-filled glove box, where the water and oxygen contents are both less than 0.1 ppm. The electrolyte we designed for this work is 2 M NaPF $_{6}$ (DoDoChem, >99.8%) dissolved in methyl propionate (MP, >99%, Macklin) and FEC (DoDoChem, >99.9%) at 9:1 (vol.%). The control electrolyte is 1 M NaPF $_{6}$ dissolved in PC (Sigma Aldrich, >99%) and FEC at 9:1 (vol.%). ### 候选资料：same-paper-1（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaTi2(PO4)3；溶剂：PYR14TFSI, PC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：PYR14TFSI=0.5, PC=0.5。 - 配方原文 [0114_0097_Electrolytes_for_electrochemical_energy::sec19::child4]：Materials Chemistry Frontiers
